C-REVIEW-ARCHIVE-SCOPE.Summary: Restrict detectZeroOrMoreSwallow and detectSelfReferential's plan loop to plans under changes/active/, using the existing scopeIdentityFromPlanRel location predicate. Leave the title regex and live-plan eagerness untouched. detectConfidentlyWrong keeps its archive scan: its <MustExist> targets assert present-tree state, while a zero-or-more-swallow (or plan-as-oracle) finding on an archived plan asserts a decision already executed. Pays F149.1. The subject finding is review.zero-or-more-swallow on archived C-REWORK-CIRCUIT T-001 (findingId d83478517d6b5e30).
C-REVIEW-ARCHIVE-SCOPE.Problem:
Registry row C-REVIEW-ARCHIVE-SCOPE in docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md (heading Named-bundle registry, named 2026-09-03 by F149.1) charters this bundle. F149 and F149.1 in the same file are the binding records. This spec does not restate them in place of those records.
F149 ratified that detectZeroOrMoreSwallow's eagerness is deliberate: the catalog remediation is to add the missing edge or rewrite titles that claim sequencing, and the one true-positive shape on record (corpus-zo-02 title "Second after first") needs the bare-word match. An id-based narrowing was measured unauthorable. That ruling stands and is not reopened.
F149.1 corrected the cost, not the count. The detector walks all of .ngrace/changes/, archives included. Archived plans are immutable and fingerprinted. gate verdict --outcome pass requires an Ack for every displayed finding. The single firing is therefore one mandatory ack on every future close, forever. Measured 2026-09-03 at HEAD 47a9b99 by parsing every plan.xml under .ngrace/changes/{active,archive} with readGraceXmlArtifact / walkNodes and the live title regex: plans=60 (0 active, 60 archive; statuses applied=54 superseded=6), tasks=297, tasksWithEmptyDependsOn=82, regexHits=1 — archive/C-REWORK-CIRCUIT T-001, status applied, title "Ceiling constant, circuit kind and state, second breaker fire, first escalation unchanged", <DependsOn> empty. F149's "1 hit in 58 plans" was true when written and is now stale (F123): two bundles archived since. The hit is unchanged. Five <Ack findingId="d83478517d6b5e30"> children already exist across three archived ledgers (C-REWORK-CIRCUIT, C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION, C-APPROVE-TIME-REVIEW).
The ratified remedy — rewrite the title — requires an editable artifact. An archived plan has none. Scoping the detector to plans that are still live restores the condition F149's ruling rests on; it does not overturn the ruling.
Three detectors walk .ngrace/changes for plan.xml (the complete set in src/review/core.ts, measured 2026-09-03): detectConfidentlyWrong's <MustExist> loop carries a status guard (skip superseded / rejected / cancelled — F123's remedy) and still scans applied archives; detectSelfReferential's plan loop (<MustMatchPattern> File targeting the plan) carries no guard; detectZeroOrMoreSwallow carries no guard. detectSelfReferential's plan loop fires on nothing in this corpus today: 0 <MustMatchPattern> nodes in 60 plans, 0 self-hits. "Fires on nothing" is a count, not a cost (F149.1's lesson). The same missing guard would make the first archive hit immortal. This bundle applies the same location filter there.
Q2, verified first: corpus-zo-02 (src/test-support/defect-corpus.ts corpus-zo-02-empty-depends-malformed-task) builds and applies at .ngrace/changes/active/C-CORPUS-ZO2/plan.xml. corpus-sr-02 (corpus-sr-02-baseline-from-plan-body) builds at .ngrace/changes/active/C-CORPUS-SR/plan.xml. An active-only location filter keeps both ratchets. The determinism gate is scripts/validate-determinism.ts: two-run identity on corpus-re-01 plus scoreCorpus() / ratchetHolds against caughtBaseline; formatCorpusScore prints per-pattern hit/total including zero-or-more-swallow: 2/2. A filter that skipped active/ would miss corpus-zo-02 and fail that ratchet.

Goals.Goal: detectZeroOrMoreSwallow inspects only plans whose path location is active (scopeIdentityFromPlanRel planLocation equals "active"). The live regex and empty-<DependsOn> predicate stay byte-identical. Sequencing titles on live plans still fire; the same title under changes/archive/ does not.
detectSelfReferential's plan loop (MustMatchPattern File targeting the plan itself) takes the same location filter in the same change. Its test-file loop is unchanged. corpus-sr-02 still fires.

detectConfidentlyWrong keeps its archive scan and its F123 status guard. A <MustExist> of a missing path on an applied archived plan still fires. This bundle states why that detector differs: it asserts present-tree state, not a decision already executed.
README.md and examples/ are unchanged; no user-visible CLI, config, or review command surface is added. The existing ngrace review command emits one fewer immortal finding.

Do not rewrite anything under .ngrace/changes/archive/.

Predicate is location, not status. scopeIdentityFromPlanRel already returns planLocation "active" | "archive" from the path .ngrace/changes/{active|archive}/<id>/plan.xml. In the applied-but-active window (status="applied" still under changes/active/, between the apply status write and the archive mv) a location filter still inspects the plan; a status skip of applied would go silent before the mv. Location is what F149.1 probed and what the corpus fixtures occupy. Status skip of applied is rejected for these two detectors: it would couple them to detectConfidentlyWrong's axis and silence a still-current change. The acceptance tests must discriminate the two predicates: archive+applied silent, active+applied fire.

Differentiation, normative: a confidently-wrong <MustExist> finding on an applied archived plan asserts something about the present tree — a shipped target should still exist — so that detector is right to keep scanning archives (F123 already dropped superseded / rejected / cancelled, whose targets are no longer present-tree obligations). A zero-or-more-swallow finding on an archived plan asserts a sequencing decision already executed: the tasks ran, in whatever order they ran, and nothing is actionable; the catalog remedy exists only while the plan is editable. detectSelfReferential's plan loop is the same class: a <MustMatchPattern> that uses the plan as its own oracle is a decision already executed, not a claim about files on disk now. That is why this change scopes those two detectors to changes/active/ and leaves detectConfidentlyWrong's archive walk in place. The two differ in what they assert, not merely in where they look.

The title regex inside detectZeroOrMoreSwallow stays byte-identical: /\bafter\b|\bsecond\b|\bthen\b|\bfollow|\bcompletes?\b|\bonce\b.*\bT-\d+/i Do not require a co-occurring \bT-\d+\b, do not drop an alternative, do not extract it to a new name as a way of editing it, and do not change severity. Live-plan eagerness is F149, ratified.

A fixture plan at .ngrace/changes/archive/C-HELDOUT-ZO/plan.xml with empty <DependsOn> and title "Second after first" (or the C-REWORK-CIRCUIT T-001 title) emits no review.zero-or-more-swallow. AcceptanceCriteria.AC-LIVE-EAGER: The same detector on a plan at .ngrace/changes/active/… with empty <DependsOn> and a sequencing title still emits review.zero-or-more-swallow. Existing FIRE zero-or-more-swallow (core.test.ts, "Runs once T-001 completes") and corpus-zo-02 (title "Second after first", mustFire true, surface review) stay green.
